IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants.summary: Mathlib supplies the two raw ingredients this roadmap builds on — Roby polynomial laws (`Mathlib/RingTheory/PolynomialLaw/Basic.lean`, definition, module structure and universe-polymorphic `toFun`/`isCompat` only) and the universal divided power algebra Γ_R(M) (`Mathlib/RingTheory/DividedPowerAlgebra/Init.lean`, with `dp`, `lift`, `map`) — plus Cayley–Hamilton for a single endomorphism (`LinearMap.aeval_self_charpoly`), lifting of complete orthogonal idempotents along nilpotent kernels, t-structures and derived categories. Tau Ceti has a genuinely large Hecke-ring development (`TauCeti/NumberTheory/HeckeRing/`, ~1100 declarations: abstract double-coset Hecke rings on top of Mathlib's `IsHeckeTriple`, associativity, commutativity, degree, GL_n coset decomposition, prime decomposition and Shimura's polynomial-ring presentation for n = 1, 2) and continuous group cohomology (`TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/`). What is genuinely missing is the entire determinant theory: no homogeneous degree-n polynomial laws, no multiplicative laws, no Chenevier determinants or pseudo-representations, no characteristic-polynomial ideal or Cayley–Hamilton quotient, no reconstruction theorem, and no Fitting ideals of modules at all (`Fitt₀` is absent from both libraries, so IHG.6's central bound cannot even be stated). The Hecke-on-complexes package (IHG.2), the spherical normalization and Hecke polynomial P_v(X) (IHG.3 — no Satake transform exists anywhere in either library), the interpolation (IHG.4) and the nilpotent descent schemas (IHG.5) are likewise absent; Tau Ceti's Hecke rings are classical GL_n(ℚ)/SL_n(ℤ) double-coset rings, not local spherical algebras with vol(K)=1.

targets.target: Polynomial laws natural in commutative coefficient algebras (Roby laws)
targets.note: Mathlib defines a polynomial law `M →ₚₗ[R] N` as a functorial family `S ⊗[R] M → S ⊗[R] N` for all R-algebras S (Roby 1963), with the universe-polymorphic extension `toFun`/`isCompat` and composition. Only `R` a CommSemiring is assumed, so this is at least as general as the layer's commutative coefficient algebras.

targets.target: Homogeneous polynomial laws of degree n and their degree decomposition
targets.note: `Mathlib/RingTheory/PolynomialLaw/` contains only `Basic.lean`; grepping it for `homogene`/`degree` finds nothing but the scalar-multiplication docstring, and no `IsHomogeneous`, coefficient or degree-n API for polynomial laws exists in either library. The file's own header says the coefficients of a polynomial law are left to 'further works'.

targets.target: Divided powers representing degree-n laws, with tensor and base-change maps
targets.note: Mathlib has the universal divided power algebra Γ_R(M) with `dp`, the weak universal property `lift`, functoriality `map`/`mapEquiv`, and divided power structures on ideals. Missing: the grading Γ^n, the representability theorem (degree-n homogeneous laws M → N ≅ Hom(Γ^n M, N)) and the base-change isomorphism S ⊗_R Γ_R(M) ≅ Γ_S(S ⊗ M) that the layer needs.

targets.target: Determinant: a multiplicative degree-n law D : A[G] → A with D(1)=1 (Chenevier determinant / pseudo-representation)
targets.note: `grep -rn -i 'pseudorepresentation|pseudo-representation|pseudocharacter|pseudo-character|Chenevier'` over both Lean trees returns nothing, and no multiplicative-polynomial-law structure exists. Mathlib's `Matrix.det`/`LinearMap.det` are multiplicative maps on actual matrices/endomorphisms, not degree-n laws on a group algebra.

targets.target: Characteristic-polynomial identities for a determinant law
targets.note: Characteristic polynomials of matrices and of endomorphisms of finite free modules are in Mathlib, but the characteristic polynomial attached to a determinant law (D(X − g) expanded in the Λ^i coefficients) presupposes the determinant, which is absent.

targets.target: Direct sum/product, duality, scalar extension, restriction to subgroups and continuity criteria for determinants
targets.note: All of these are operations on determinant laws, which do not exist in either library; nothing analogous appears under `PolynomialLaw`.

targets.target: Agreement with the matrix determinant for a rank-n finite projective representation
targets.note: `LinearMap.det` is defined for endomorphisms of an arbitrary module (via a basis when one exists, 1 otherwise) and is multiplicative; but the comparison statement 'the determinant law of a rank-n finite projective representation is g ↦ det(ρ g)' cannot be stated without the determinant law.

targets.target: Trace comparison in the valid coefficient range (n! invertible)
targets.note: No trace/determinant reconstruction statement (Taylor's theorem that pseudo-characters and determinants agree when n! is invertible) exists in either library.

duplicates.note: R01.5 ('Recognition by Frobenius polynomials') explicitly consumes 'the arbitrary-degree multiplicative polynomial laws, Cayley–Hamilton algebras and representation theorem of IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants', so it is a declared consumer rather than a competing owner; the overlap is only in the rank-two trace/determinant specialisation.

targets.target: Characteristic-polynomial ideal and Cayley–Hamilton quotient of an algebra with a determinant
targets.note: Mathlib proves Cayley–Hamilton for a single endomorphism of a finite free module (`aeval_self_charpoly`), which is the classical statement; Chenevier's CH(A,D) ideal generated by the values of the characteristic polynomial law, and the quotient algebra, are absent — grep for `CharpolyIdeal`, `CayleyHamilton` as an algebra structure returns nothing.

targets.target: Faithful determinant descent (a determinant descends to the CH quotient faithfully)
targets.note: Depends on determinants, which do not exist in either library.

targets.target: Generalized matrix algebra decomposition under residual multiplicity-freeness
targets.note: `grep -i 'GeneralizedMatrixAlgebra|generalized_matrix'` over declarations.tsv and both Lean trees finds nothing; Mathlib's `Matrix.fromBlocks` machinery is only the block-matrix calculus, not the GMA structure with its idempotents and bimodule entries.

targets.target: Reconstruction of a representation from a determinant over an algebraically closed field, up to semisimplification
targets.note: Nothing in either library reconstructs a representation from a determinant/pseudo-character; Mathlib's character theory (`Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Character.lean`) proves linear independence and equality-of-characters results over fields of characteristic zero only, not the degree-n determinant statement.

targets.target: Reconstruction over a complete local ring under residual absolute irreducibility
targets.note: Absent, for the same reason; there is no theory of residually absolutely irreducible lifts in either tree.

targets.target: Residual reducibility and lifting obstructions
targets.note: No reducibility-obstruction API exists.

targets.target: Reducibility ideals, extension modules and lattice constructions for congruences
targets.note: Reducibility ideals are absent. Mathlib has `Ext` in abelian categories, `groupCohomology`, and (new) continuous cohomology of a topological group in `Mathlib/RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/`, which Tau Ceti extends with restriction/inflation/corestriction, Shapiro and long exact sequences; so H¹ classifying extensions is available in general form. The arithmetic lattice and reducibility-ideal package is not.

duplicates.note: Declared consumer of exactly this layer's Cayley–Hamilton algebras and representation theorem; it adds Chebotarev density and coefficient descent rather than restating them.
AG2.3 lists IHG.1 among its dependencies and applies the reconstruction step; the overlap is in the use, not the construction.

R19.6 'Representations over Hecke algebras' constructs the determinant law from Hecke operators and proves representability under residual absolute irreducibility — the same reconstruction theorem, instantiated at a localised completed Hecke algebra.

targets.target: Hecke action on a bounded perfect complex and its finite image algebras
targets.note: Mathlib defines abstract Hecke rings of a Hecke pair/triple and Tau Ceti builds the ring structure, GL_n instance and coset calculus on top; but no action of a Hecke ring on a complex, and no notion of 'image algebra in End of a complex', appears in either library. The `line` for `IntegralHeckeRing` could not be pinned in declarations.tsv; the definition is in the cited file's final section.

targets.target: Perfect complexes over a commutative ring, bounded amplitude
targets.note: `grep -i 'PerfectComplex'` finds nothing in either tree. Mathlib has `HomologicalComplex`, `CochainComplex`, `DerivedCategory` and `CategoryTheory.Triangulated`, but no perfect-complex predicate.

targets.target: Comparison of chain, homotopy/derived and cohomology actions
targets.note: Mathlib has the derived category, the homotopy category and the homology functors, so the three targets of the comparison exist as categories; the statement comparing the three images of a fixed Hecke algebra is absent.

targets.target: Localization decompositions over complete coefficient rings; support and annihilator lemmas; finite generation
targets.note: Mathlib lifts complete orthogonal idempotents along a nilpotent-kernel surjection, which is the key ingredient for decomposing a finite algebra over a complete local ring into local factors; the decomposition statement for a semilocal complete algebra, and the associated support/annihilator lemmas for a Hecke action, are not formulated.

targets.target: Nilpotence bound for the ideal of degree-zero derived endomorphisms acting trivially on all cohomology of a bounded-amplitude object, via the t-structure filtration
targets.note: The t-structure machinery the proof needs (truncations, the standard t-structure on the derived category, its heart) is in Mathlib, but the nilpotence statement itself — that an endomorphism inducing zero on every cohomology object of an amplitude-[a,b] object has (b−a+1)-st power zero — is absent from both trees.

targets.target: Transport of the nilpotence bound to Hecke images, preserving the amplitude dependence
targets.note: Depends on the previous two targets; absent.

duplicates.note: TC.2 is the declared consumer of this layer's nilpotence bound for actual arithmetic complexes; it supplies the geometric comparison rather than reproving the abstract bound.

R19.6 asks for 'nilpotent structure and the distinction between reduced characteristic-zero specialisations and the whole integral Hecke algebra' — the same nilpotent-ideal phenomenon, but for the completed Hecke algebra of a fixed automorphic setting.

targets.target: The unramified local Hecke algebra of GL_n at v with T_{v,i} = char. function of K diag(ϖ^i,1^{n−i}) K and vol(K)=1
targets.note: Tau Ceti's `HeckeRing.GLn` builds exactly the classical global-integral analogues: the diagonal double cosets T(p,…,p,1,…,1) as `heckeGen k`, the p-local subring and Shimura's presentation. But this is the Hecke ring of the pair (SL_n(ℤ), integral matrices of positive determinant) inside GL_n(ℚ), built from finite double-coset counting; there is no local field, no hyperspecial K with a Haar measure normalised by vol(K)=1, and no p-adic group in either library.

targets.target: The Hecke polynomial P_v(X) = Σ (−1)^i q_v^{i(i−1)/2} T_{v,i} X^{n−i} with T_{v,0}=1
targets.note: `grep -rn -i 'hecke polynomial'` over both Lean trees returns nothing, and the q^{i(i−1)/2} coefficient pattern does not occur. Tau Ceti's `GLn/PolynomialRing` is a presentation of the Hecke ring as ℤ[X₁,…,X_n], a different object from this generating polynomial in X with Hecke coefficients.

targets.target: Normalized Satake transform and the isomorphism with the Weyl-invariant algebra
targets.note: `grep -rn -i 'satake'` over `mathlib/Mathlib/` and `TauCeti/TauCeti/` returns zero hits; the layer's SR.4 prerequisite is itself unbuilt.

targets.target: Relation of P_v to the determinant character and Tate twist
targets.note: Requires both the Satake transform and the determinant of IHG.0; neither exists.

targets.target: Explicit conversion theorems between conventions (arithmetic/geometric Frobenius, inverse roots)
targets.note: Tau Ceti has arithmetic Frobenius at a prime of a number field (`NumberField.Chebotarev.isArithFrobAt` and the Artin symbol API under `TauCeti/NumberTheory/Chebotarev/`), but no dictionary relating Frobenius conventions to a Hecke polynomial.

targets.target: Verification at n=1 against class field theory and at n=2 against the classical modular-form Hecke polynomial
targets.note: Tau Ceti proves the n = 1 and n = 2 cases of Shimura's Theorem 3.20 (surjectivity of ℤ[X₁,X₂] ↠ R_p) and has the GL₂ Hecke recurrence T(p^{k+1}) = T(p)T(p^k) − p·T(p^{k−1})·⟨p⟩-type relations, which is the classical n = 2 content the layer wants checked; the check itself, against a Hecke polynomial that does not exist, cannot be stated. Tau Ceti's own file header records that general n needs two further unformalised steps.

duplicates.note: SR.4 owns the Satake transform and states it will 'provide the normalization dictionary consumed by IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants'; the two layers share the normalisation conventions, with SR.4 the declared owner of Satake itself.

AG2.0 constructs 'the normalization dictionary among algebraic weights, geometric/arithmetic Frobenius, cyclotomic twists, normalized Satake and the integral Hecke polynomial of IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.3' — the same dictionary, cited to this layer.
TC.3 works with the same ambient Hecke polynomial and Levi Satake map for boundary induction, and factors it; it consumes rather than restates the normalisation.

targets.target: Compatible determinants over finite coefficient quotients from a dense family of classical Hecke systems
targets.note: Determinants do not exist in either library (see IHG.0), so no interpolation statement can be formulated.

targets.target: Uniqueness from Frobenius density via Chebotarev and continuity
targets.note: Tau Ceti has a substantial Chebotarev tree (Frobenius prime sets, the Artin symbol, tagged fixed fields, Galois-character orthogonality, von Mangoldt prime counting) but the density theorem is still under construction there, and in any case the uniqueness statement it would feed — that two continuous determinants agreeing on Frobenius elements coincide — presupposes determinants.

targets.target: Existence by polynomial-law identities on the completed group algebra
targets.note: `grep -i 'completedGroup|CompletedGroupAlgebra|iwasawaAlgebra|ProfiniteGroupAlgebra'` over declarations.tsv returns nothing; the completed group algebra ℤ_p[[G]] of a profinite group is not in either library, let alone polynomial-law identities on it.

targets.target: Change-of-level, change-of-coefficients and passage to inverse limits for determinants
targets.note: Absent for the same reason. Mathlib's `Module.topologicalClosure`/inverse-limit machinery exists generically but is not applied here.

targets.target: Retention of the finite ramification set and continuity hypotheses
targets.note: No API for Galois representations/determinants unramified outside a finite set S exists in either library.

duplicates.note: R01.5 owns the Chebotarev recognition side of the same uniqueness statement (semisimple representations determined by characteristic polynomials at Frobenius), while IHG.4 owns the determinant-valued interpolation; they overlap on the density argument.
Constructs a determinant law from Hecke operators and Frobenius polynomials over a completed Hecke algebra — the concrete instance of this layer's abstract interpolation.
Declared consumer: it feeds an equivariant Igusa boundary Hecke polynomial into this interpolation.

targets.target: Theorem schemas taking a geometric Hecke comparison with a quantified nilpotent error ideal to a determinant in the appropriate quotient
targets.note: Neither the determinants (IHG.0) nor the nilpotent-ideal bounds (IHG.2) exist, so the schema has no components to combine.

targets.target: Functoriality and nilpotence bounds under products and extensions
targets.note: Mathlib has a complete general theory of nilpotent elements and nilpotent ideals with the usual closure properties, which is the ambient algebra; the specific nilpotence-index bookkeeping for Hecke error ideals under products and extensions is not present.

targets.target: Specialization to residual semisimple representations
targets.note: Semisimplification of a representation over a field is not in either library in the form needed (Mathlib has `Module.IsSemisimple` and Jordan–Hölder via `CompositionSeries`, but no residual semisimplification functor for Galois representations), and the determinant-valued statement is absent.

targets.target: Local conditions on extension classes and comparison of lattice choices for congruence applications
targets.note: Continuous group cohomology exists (Mathlib's `ContinuousCohomology`, extended in `TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Homological/ContCohomology/` with restriction, inflation, corestriction, Shapiro and the long exact sequence), so the extension classes have a home; but no local conditions on Galois extension classes and no lattice-comparison results exist.

duplicates.note: TC.2 builds the geometric Hecke comparison with its nilpotent error that this layer consumes as a hypothesis; the nilpotence bookkeeping is shared.

AutomorphicCongruences owns the congruence-module/Selmer-class side and the automorphic lower bounds; this layer's 'local conditions of extension classes and lattice choices' is the same material seen from the abstract side.

targets.target: Fitting ideals Fitt₀_T(M) of a finitely generated module and their functoriality
targets.note: Neither library has Fitting ideals: `grep -rn -i 'fitting ideal|fittingIdeal|Fitt_'` over both Lean trees returns nothing, and every `Fitting` hit in declarations.tsv is the Lie-theoretic Fitting decomposition (`LieModule.posFittingComp`). Since the central conclusion of both DKSW theorems is a Fitting-ideal containment, the layer cannot even be stated today.

targets.target: Rank-two continuous representation over the total quotient ring K of a complete reduced Noetherian local T, with characteristic polynomials in T[X]
targets.note: The ambient commutative algebra is present (total quotient rings via `IsLocalization` at non-zero-divisors, `IsLocalRing`, `IsNoetherianRing`, `IsAdicComplete`), and continuous cohomology of a topological group with topological coefficients is now in Mathlib and extended by Tau Ceti. What is missing is the representation-theoretic setup: continuous rank-two representations into GL₂ of a total quotient ring, their field-factor projections, and the characteristic-polynomial integrality hypothesis.

targets.target: Construction of the finite T-module M and the class in H¹(G, M(χ/ψ)) every cocycle of which generates M, with Fitt₀_T(M) ⊆ I
targets.note: Mathlib's `ContinuousCohomology` (with Tau Ceti's restriction/inflation/Shapiro/long-exact-sequence layer on top) provides the H¹ in which the class would live — the roadmap assigns that API to ArithmeticGaloisDuality. The theorem itself, the generalised Ribet lemma of Dasgupta–Kakde–Silliman–Wang Theorem 1.1 with residual indistinguishability allowed, is absent.

targets.target: The local-condition version for T ⊂ T̃ with the product bound (∏_{v∈P}(ξ_v(σ_v) − χ(σ_v)))·Fitt₀_T(N) ⊆ Ĩ
targets.note: DKSW Theorem 2.1; absent, and again not statable without Fitting ideals.

targets.target: Formal matrix ring with trace/determinant invariants and the integral matrix-invariant theorem
targets.note: Traces and determinants of matrices over a commutative ring are in Mathlib, but the invariant theory of the formal 2×2 matrix ring over ℤ (generation of the invariants of GL₂ acting on matrix tuples by traces and determinants, integrally) is not; `grep -i 'invariant theory|first fundamental theorem'` finds nothing relevant in either tree.

targets.target: Rational (algebraic-group) cohomology restriction and acyclicity statements
targets.note: Neither library has cohomology of representations of an affine algebraic group scheme (Hochschild/rational cohomology); Mathlib's `groupCohomology` is for abstract groups and Tau Ceti's `ContCohomology` for topological groups. Tau Ceti does have affine algebraic group schemes (`TauCeti/Algebra/AlgebraicGroup/`) and comodules, but not their cohomology.

targets.target: Koszul and Buchsbaum–Rim complexes with grade/regularity hypotheses and exactness
targets.note: Mathlib has regular sequences, their behaviour under flat base change and localisation, and a Rees-style depth characterisation via vanishing Ext. It has no Koszul complex (`grep -i 'koszul complex|KoszulComplex'` returns nothing; every `koszul` hit in Tau Ceti is the Koszul sign rule in graded/monoidal homological algebra) and no Buchsbaum–Rim complex.

duplicates.note: I.7 states it will 'import the general representation/lattice/extension-class/annihilator theorem from IntegralHeckeAndGaloisDeterminants IHG.6, including this residual coincidence case', and verifies the Hilbert/Eisenstein hypotheses; the generalised Ribet lemma is stated in both but owned here.
I.6 builds the Ritter–Weiss modules and 'their Fitting-ideal functoriality' — the same missing Fitting-ideal API that this layer needs for Fitt₀_T(M) ⊆ I.
A readiness checkpoint aggregating I.6 and I.7, explicitly including 'the residually indistinguishable representation-theoretic proof'; it is bookkeeping over the same theorem.
ES.7 'Higher-rank derivatives and Fitting-ideal control' needs the same absent Fitting-ideal API, though for Kolyvagin systems rather than Ribet classes.
